refs.quote: MESTINON (pyridostigmine bromide) is an orally active cholinesterase inhibitor. Chemically, pyridostigmine bromide is 3-hydroxy-1-methylpyridinium bromide dimethylcarbamate.

tall_man.note: Not listed in FDA/ISMP Tall Man list; generic name lowercase per EXTRACTION.md

refs.quote: MESTINON is useful in the treatment of myasthenia gravis. === DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION === DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION: MESTINON is available in three dosage forms: Oral Solution - raspberry-flavored,
Conventional tablets - The average dose is ten 60 mg tablets or ten 5 mL teaspoonfuls daily, spaced to provide maximum relief when maximum strength is needed.

regimens.dose_text: Initial: 60 mg orally every 4 to 6 hours while awake. Adjust size and frequency of dose to clinical response. Average dose is 600 mg daily (ten 60 mg tablets). Timespan 180 mg 1-2 times daily may be used at bedtime for nocturnal/morning symptoms.

mg_safety.note: First-line symptomatic therapy for myasthenia gravis; distinguish cholinergic crisis (overdose) from myasthenic crisis (underdose)

value.instructions: Conventional 60 mg tablets may be crushed; oral solution (60 mg/5 mL) is available and easily administered via tube. TIMESPAN extended-release tablets must NOT be crushed or chewed.

refs.quote: TIMESPAN tablets - each containing 180 mg pyridostigmine bromide.
ADVERSE REACTIONS: The side effects of MESTINON are most commonly related to overdosage and generally are of two varieties, muscarinic and nicotinic.

mechanism_of_action.value: Reversibly inhibits acetylcholinesterase, prolonging the action of acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction.

refs.quote: ACTIONS: MESTINON inhibits the destruction of acetylcholine by cholinesterase and thereby permits freer transmission of nerve impulses across the neuromuscular junction.

value.metabolism: hydrolyzed by cholinesterases; minor hepatic microsomal metabolism
